ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, for the square $ABCD$ with side length $2$, where point $E$ is the midpoint of side $BC$, and point $P$ moves along the diagonal $AC$, what is the minimum value of $PE+PB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw line DE, intersecting AC at point P, and draw BD. \\
$\because$ Point B and point D are symmetric about AC, \\
$\therefore$ DP=PB, \\
$\therefore$ PB+PE=PD+PE=DE \\
$\therefore$ The length of DE is the minimum value of PE+PB, \\
$\because$ In the square ABCD, AB=2, and E is the midpoint of BC, \\
$\therefore$ CE=1, \\
In $\triangle CDE$, \\
DE=$\sqrt{CD^{2}+CE^{2}}$ \\
=$\sqrt{2^{2}+1^{2}}$ \\
=$\sqrt{5}$ \\
Hence, the answer is: $\boxed{\sqrt{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a square ABCD, A is at the lower left, B is at the lower right, C is at the upper right, D is at the upper left; diagonal AC is drawn, point P is located on diagonal AC; point E is on the right side BC, and the problem statement explains that E is the midpoint of BC; the figure also marks line segments PB and PE. Since the sum of distances along a line segment is a convex function, the interior critical point gives the minimum value. Substitute t=4/3, PE=sqrt((-2/3)^2+(1/3)^2)=sqrt(5)/3, PB=sqrt((-2/3)^2+(4/3)^2)=2sqrt(5)/3, so PE+PB=sqrt(5).
